title: Pointed evaluation lands in the relative separable closure
statement: Let Y be a scheme, barY: Spec Ω → Y an algebraically closed geometric point, and give Ω the residue-field algebra structure specified by barY (hΩ). For every a in the chosen coordinate-ring colimit C [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], its canonical pointed evaluation [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation] in Ω belongs to the relative separable closure of the residue field of the image of barY [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. No local-ring hypothesis on C is required.

proof.text: Cofilteredness of the representative category and preservation of filtered colimits by the forgetful functor give a representative b at one neighbourhood for each colimit element (Concrete.colimit_exists_rep).
The colimit coprojection equation and residue_descResidueField identify the evaluation with the geometric residue embedding applied to the global-section residue of b.

The etale neighbourhood residue extension is separable. Its embedding into Ω preserves separability (IsSeparable.map). The pointed factorization identifies the base points and, by hΩ, the base algebra maps; IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv transports across residueFieldCongr. mem_separableClosure_iff gives the claim.
